curation.reason: Focus the current collection on the strongest basin-density, growing-deficit Fourier, sharp Syracuse integrability and positive stationary-envelope results. Removal of earlier papers is an editorial choice and does not declare their checked results false.
removed_from_current_collection: Two-coordinate obstruction paper and its standalone formal development
Independent second proof of Said Duran's equal-height theorem and its standalone formal development

limitations: Sublinear masked cylinder energy, equivalently universal eventual periodicity, remains unresolved. The equivalence does not exclude additional cycles.
The raw occupation lower bound supplies no matching raw upper bound or convergence of the normalized sum; it does not exclude divergent orbits.

The inverse height clock is almost sure at each fixed positive odd nonperiodic unit root; no expected occupation limit or uniform integrability follows. The divergent-excess theorem retains the hypothetical injective orbit as an assumption.
The lower-bound constants are fixed Lean choices; no numerical value or uniform finite-cutoff estimate is asserted.
Novelty comparisons and automated semantic reviews are not external peer review or an exhaustive priority search.
Verification scope is stated per record; source/object authentication is distinguished from fresh compilation and individual kernel replay.
The Fourier result concerns finite random affine laws with a growing but sublinear deficit; its ineffective constants and conditioning ranges do not supply a deterministic Collatz orbit estimate.

The sharp Syracuse integrability theorem concerns full additive Haar measure and gives no integer trace estimate, weak-L2 endpoint, exact linear energy asymptotic or Collatz convergence result. External compiled libraries in its full internal replay are an explicitly stated reuse boundary.

The positive stationary envelope identifies the arithmetic trace at each fixed positive integer and gives uniform cylinder lower bounds; it does not supply a uniform moving-root approximation, expected occupation upper bound, cycle exclusion or Collatz convergence.

papers.additional_results: Uniform exact first-hit coefficient bound at positive odd targets, including periodic targets; actual finite cylinder-mass transport and energy decomposition; an exact finite-energy criterion equivalent to universal eventual periodicity, with unconditional normalized decay outside every diverging ancestor barrier. Unconditional raw occupation lower bound: for every b<1/log(4/3), the sum of actual weighted first-hit densities over odd N≤R is at least b log R for all sufficiently large integer R. A specified injective odd orbit forces the additional lower coefficient D_u/(P_infinity(u)*log(3/2)), strictly positive at unit roots. Under the actual inverse Doob law at every positive odd nonperiodic unit root, log(Y_k)/k tends almost surely to log(4/3).
papers.credit: The inverse-linear form was proposed by Wirsching. The proof uses Mazur's weighted predecessor construction and Said Duran's coalescence theorem, alongside the density and canonical-limit foundations described in the paper.
papers.main_result: For one fixed positive integer K_seed and every positive target N prime to three, shortcut and ordinary predecessor natural densities are at least 3/(128*K_seed*N).
papers.title: Collatz basin densities and canonical traces from first-passage stabilization

papers.additional_results: Conditioning on total-exponent slices with polynomially bounded reciprocal mass preserves superpolynomial decay for n-k<=k^beta, 0<beta<1. The central slice S_k=2k has mass at least 1/(4k) for k>=1 and satisfies that decay conclusion for k>=4.
papers.credit: Tao's full-length endpoint is prior work. The comparison with Si is confined to his stated central-slice logarithmic oversampling range. The proof incorporates the credited Subspace Theorem formalizations and renewal inputs.
papers.limitations: Constants are ineffective. No conductor-power decay at fixed positive deficit ratio, deterministic integer transfer, or Collatz convergence result is asserted.
papers.main_result: For every fixed natural A, primitive Fourier coefficients of the k-step geometric Syracuse affine law modulo 3^n are bounded by C_A*((n-k+2)/n)^A for n>=1 and 0<=k<=n, uniformly in the seed and in unit-modulus phases depending on the total exponent.
papers.title: Fourier decay for truncated Syracuse affine laws

papers.additional_results: Uniform finite-level Lp bounds for every real 1<=p<2; the actual stationary density equation; failure of L2 through positive support overlap. The depth-zero and p=1 finite-level boundary cases are assembled from the named public endpoints explained in the theorem map.
papers.credit: Tao supplies the random law, fine-scale mixing and fixed-length/fixed-total offset injectivity. The quadratic energy argument uses distinct natural quotients and normalized geometric moments. No exhaustive priority claim is made.
papers.limitations: These are random-law Haar estimates. No weak-L2 bound, exact linear energy growth, integer trace estimate or individual-orbit convergence result is asserted.
papers.main_result: For the canonical fair Syracuse law on the 3-adic integers, full-Haar depth-k cylinder energy is at most 24k+8k^2<=32k^2 for k>=1. One normalized nonnegative density has exact real Lp range 1<=p<2.
papers.title: Quadratic cylinder energy and integrability of the Syracuse law

papers.additional_results: Every unit cylinder of depth k has mass at least c*3^(-k), and the minimum-cylinder logarithmic exponent is one. At each positive integer the cylinder densities converge to the arithmetic trace in Cesaro mean absolute error. Infinite values form a Haar-null G-delta dense in the units; the finite trace is unbounded among positive odd integers in every unit residue class, and the envelope is discontinuous at every positive unit integer.
papers.credit: Tao supplies the stationary law, first-passage framework and minimum-cylinder question. The arithmetic inputs come from the companion basin-density development with its distinct Mazur and Said Duran attribution. The comparison with Nikpour and Rabbani is limited to the upper bound reported in their preprint; no exhaustive priority claim is made.
papers.limitations: The integer statements are pointwise in the root. No uniform moving-root approximation, ordinary pointwise convergence of individual cylinder densities, expected occupation upper bound, cycle exclusion or forward Collatz convergence is asserted.
papers.main_result: The canonical Syracuse stationary probability on the 3-adic integers has a greatest nonnegative lower semicontinuous density for full additive Haar probability. It integrates to one, vanishes off the units, has a uniform positive lower bound on the units, and equals the actual weighted first-hit arithmetic trace at every positive integer, including periodic targets.
papers.title: A positive semicontinuous density for the Syracuse stationary law
